newsitem.title: ITALY: Judge asks Italian high court to rule on ex-Nazi.
newsitem.headline: Judge asks Italian high court to rule on ex-Nazi.

text.p: A judge asked Italy's highest court on Tuesday to decide whether former Nazi Erich Priebke should be tried in a civilian or military court for the country's worst World War Two atrocity.

The war crimes case against the former SS captain was left without a court on December 15 after a civilian prosecutor said he had no jurisdiction and asked Rome preliminary investigating judge Ciro Monsurro to rule on the matter.
Monsurro on Tuesday asked the Cassation Court, Italy's highest court, to decide whether a military or civilian court should try Priebke.

Priebke, 83, is accused of complicity in multiple murder for his acknowledged participation in the Ardeatine Caves massacre south of Rome in March 1944, when 335 men and boys were shot in reprisal for a partisan bomb attack.
Priebke has faced a military court in Rome, but the trial, dogged by legal challenges, ended in uproar in August when the court found him guilty but ruled he was no longer liable for punishment.
The verdict was later overturned and a new trial ordered.
Italian judges have also renewed a detention order against Priebke and former SS major Karl Hass, whose trial is being sought in Italy for the same atrocity, paramilitary police said on Tuesday.
A handful of supporters of Priebke held a special mass on Monday night in Rome to pray for the former SS captain.
Both he and Hass argue they were under orders to take part in the massacre and would have been killed had they refused.
